hooks.description: Emit paths and versions of common dev tools so the agent does not burn round-trips discovering them

Detect test-weakening transitions (TestDepth escalation, tolerance widening, dimension shrinkage) by comparing old vs new text — the in-session mirror of tools/ci/agent-protection/detect-test-hiding.sh
Announce, on-record, any edit to integrity-enforcement infrastructure (agent-protection detectors, .claude hooks, CI workflows) so a quiet weakening cannot pass unnoticed
Block the AskUserQuestion multiple-choice tool — broken in the current Claude Code version; ask in plain text instead
Soft nudge the agent to call memory_store (or consultant remember) when a long stretch of work has happened without one — see docs/plans/MEMORY_REMINDER_HOOK.md
Block git commit — agents stage only, humans commit
Block 'git worktree add' — all changes must stay in the single working tree the developer can see (read-only 'git worktree list' allowed)
Block 'git worktree add' — all changes must stay in the single working tree the developer can see (read-only 'git worktree list' allowed)
Warn when an artifact-producing mvn command (compile/install/etc.) is run, since it will not rebuild dependent modules; report ~/.m2 artifact staleness
Block direct mvn test — must use mcp__ar-test-runner__start_test_run
Block bash manipulation of checkstyle configuration (checkstyle.xml, checkstyle-suppressions.xml, any /checkstyle/ dir, etc.) — abandon the task rather than tamper with enforcement
Block simple `ls <path>` / `grep <pattern> <file>` — use the structured `glob` / `grep` tools instead (compound shell features are allowed through)
Block shell writes into ~/.claude/projects/*/memory/ — use ar-manager
Warn on `git log` — workstream narrative lives in memory_branch_context, not commit titles

Block raw shell reads (find/grep/cat/ls) of generated compiler output — instruction-set dumps, *.metal/*.cl kernels, OperationProfile XML — and steer to the ar-profile-analyzer MCP tool (list_profiles/search_operations/get_source)
Block creating/tracking/pushing a non-master branch against remote master/main (the 'branch tracks origin/master' footgun) — use --no-track or branch off local master
Inject .github/CLAUDE.md context when reading analysis.yaml
Inject bidirectional dependency check when reading any pom.xml
Block edits adding a run of 4+ consecutive inline // comment lines - CLAUDE.md forbids excessive inline comments
Block edits to checkstyle configuration — abandon the task rather than tamper with enforcement
Block dependency/module/parent structural changes in pom.xml — dependency graph is externally controlled (non-structural edits pass through)
Warn if consult not called before editing computation-layer Java
Inject .github/CLAUDE.md context when editing analysis.yaml
Validate analysis.needs includes all coverage-* uploaders before edit
Warn on added defensive-tolerance patterns (see .claude/hooks/rules/fail-loud.md)
Block reflective method invocation (getDeclaredMethod/Method.invoke) in Java edits — call the method directly; mirror of the ReflectiveInvocationDetector CI gate

Verdict on ~/.m2 artifact staleness before the test runner or build validator invokes Maven out-of-band — these MCP tools bypass the Bash hook, which is exactly how stale artifacts from a previous branch produced false local test results

Remind the agent on EVERY new Java method it introduces: place it at the most general location where it makes sense (the generality ladder), with a sharper second tier when the method is static — the agent's trained-in first instinct is reliably procedural and short-termist

Detect interface-contract bypass in Java edits: BLOCK new members that re-expose a concrete class the constructor adapts behind an interface (the getStemOutput pattern), warn on abstraction-level forks (getStemOutput beside getStem) and new instanceof checks against repo classes — an API that traffics in an interface must stay correct for every implementation
Check repo_url/branch arguments to ar-manager against live git — block writes on mismatch, warn on reads. ar-manager runs remotely and cannot verify the caller's working tree itself.
Warn when a just-read source file (java/py/ts/etc.) reaches 1480 lines — recommended max 1500, checkstyle hard limit 1600 (build fails beyond); a refactor signal, not a compaction target
Scan written Java for Producer pattern violations (.evaluate/.toDouble/.toFloat in computation code, for+setMem loops, System.out/err, multiple new Model())
Warn on @Test methods with no assertion (see .claude/hooks/rules/fail-loud.md)
Warn on line-number references in source comments (e.g. Foo.java:123, 'line 660-664') — they go stale on the next edit
